checklist.action: write analysis to .pipeline-state/<branch>-analysis.md so later stages can read it
preserve ALL existing behavior — no functional changes
if analysis specifies tests, write them — refactors that change structure need tests proving behavior is preserved
cross-ref analysis test list against actual tests written
write list of all changed files to .pipeline-state/<branch>-changes.txt (git diff --name-only HEAD)

sibling sweep — when the root cause is a SHAPE (a stale value read by more than one consumer, a guard applied at one call site, a claim about one exit path), enumerate every other instance of that shape and state for each whether it needs the same fix. v0.5.2 shipped this defect three times: #24's stale mirror was guarded for the undo consumer but not the mutate consumer; crossMoveTarget was cleared while addPlaylist ten lines away was only hidden; a 'fires only on X' KDoc missed the rollback exit path. Each was caught a review round later, in the fix's own diff.

checklist._note: MANDATORY --rerun-tasks (or clear the results dirs): Gradle UP-TO-DATE caching silently degraded this stage into a replay in PR #23. Parse the JUnit XML for counts — a console summary is not evidence.

checklist.action: run full test suite (read-only, no source modifications)
execute the plan's manual test matrix where feasible; record pass/skip(reason) per row and post evidence for executed rows as a PR comment

algebra-core features (compaction/netting/merge rules): the manual matrix needs one row per algebra rule that composes with a user-visible operation (undo, retry, refresh) — not just one row per gesture

emulator UI automation: script interactions as atomic chains (full gesture sequence, then end-state verification via files + UI dump); per-step tap-verify loops race sheet animations and snackbar timers

every manual-matrix row carries a Requires: field (device / emulator / desktop script / none). Rows that require nothing but a script MUST be executed here, not deferred — PR #34's desktop round-trip was discharged this way after two milestones of deferral. A row that a plan names as the SOLE mitigation for a risk becomes a named blocking carry, never a silent skip.

verify the INSTRUMENT before believing its verdict — a harness that reports someone else's exit code, or a discriminator that cannot actually discriminate, produces confident false verification. Check: exit codes come from the command under test (never from a pipeline's last element — `cmd | tail` reports tail's status); a value used to tell two cases apart is validated against a case where the answer is known. v0.5.2 lost this four times in its own verification runs: `| tail` twice, file mtime as a write-vs-sync discriminator twice.
cross-ref analysis plan vs refactoring — flag unimplemented changes
read .pipeline-state/<branch>-analysis.md to understand what was refactored
discover project docs structure (read docs/README.md or index)
add/update docstrings for modified public APIs
update existing docs that reference moved/renamed code
verify no broken internal links or orphaned docs

if this change adds/renames/removes an enumerated unit (skill, CLI/slash command, plugin, make target, item in a 'supported X' list), update EVERY inventory/index doc that lists its siblings — grep a sibling's name across non-source files to find them; DOCS_ONLY does not exempt this

if any stage corrected a FACTUAL claim during this run (a review finding, a mutation result that contradicted a comment), grep `docs/` and `CHANGELOG.md` for the same claim before committing. A false claim that reached documentation outlives the comment that spawned it — PR #29's forced-locale rationale was corrected in code while the copy in `docs/spec.md` survived a full fix pass.

strike this task's ROADMAP priority-matrix row and add the ✅ shipped note to its milestone section — scripts/release-ready.sh reads those rows, so an unstruck row for merged work makes the release gate report work that is already done

quantifier audit: grep the PROSE diff of this run (CHANGELOG, KDoc, commit/PR bodies, test comments) for `always`, `never`, `every`, `all`, `cannot`, `since`, `has emitted`, `structurally`. Each hit either names the executed evidence for its scope or gets narrowed. PR #43 shipped four false prose claims over correct code; all were quantifier or transcription failures

derive, never transcribe: any number in prose that a command can produce (test counts, row counts, sizes) must be re-derived by running the command at the commit that ships the text. PR #50's `:core 89` baseline was correct in the artifact it was copied from and wrong where it landed

any claim about another repository's history ("the exporter has always X") must cite a sha and the command that found it — both cross-repo claims in PR #43 back-projected today's code into the past, and both were wrong

any claim that something exists in an external system (an issue filed, a PR merged, a file or symbol present in another repo) must be verified by running the command that would find it, at commit time. Three v0.5.1 instances of the forward-dated claim — a plan stated as fact — and the quantifier audit is structurally blind to all of them (no quantifier)
read .pipeline-state/<branch>-changes.txt for list of files modified by refactor
git remote -v — verify github remote exists
git add -u to stage ALL modified tracked files
git add each file from changes.txt to catch new files
verify PR body against actual diff — no phantom features, wrong counts, or incorrect terminology; fix with gh pr edit if needed

9.name: Code Review
9.subagent_prompt: You are reviewing PR #{pr_number} for a refactor. Project: {project_path}. PR targets {pr_target_branch}. Step 0: Read .pipeline-state/*-analysis.md for the original analysis. Step 1: Run git diff {pr_target_branch}...HEAD, read changed files. Check docs/PULL_REQUEST_CHECKLIST.md if exists. Step 2: Cross-ref analysis vs implementation — verify all planned changes were made. CRITICAL: Verify behavior is preserved — refactor must NOT change functionality. Step 3: Review for correctness, security, testing, quality, docs, perf. Flag auto-reject triggers. Step 4: Run project test suite, report pass/fail. Step 5: Decide APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES/COMMENT. Step 6 MANDATORY: Post review to GitHub with gh pr review {pr_number} --comment --body '<formatted review>'. If REQUEST_CHANGES use --request-changes. Save to pr/feedback/ if dir exists. Step 7: Output verdict. Step FINAL (MANDATORY, #36): you are read-only — restore the executor's working tree before returning. Capture your starting branch first (START=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)); on exit run `git checkout "$START"` and verify `git status --porcelain` is clean (`git restore --staged --worktree .` + `git clean -fd` (remove untracked files you created) if you dirtied it). NEVER leave the tree on {pr_target_branch} or with reverted/staged files — a build/scp the executor runs next would ship stale content.

checklist.action: load project PR checklist if exists (docs/PULL_REQUEST_CHECKLIST.md)
cross-ref analysis vs implementation — all planned changes made
verify behavior preserved — refactor must NOT change functionality
review: correctness, security, testing, quality, docs, perf

mutation-test the claims: for any row naming a production mechanism as its subject, delete or invert that mechanism and confirm the row FAILS. A mutation table must mark each entry APPLIED (executed, with observed failures) or PREDICTED (a claim) — PR #34 found two uncovered branches hiding in the PREDICTED column. Execute a sample of the PREDICTED entries; one that kills nothing is a coverage gap or an equivalent mutant, and you must say which. Driver hygiene: run every evaluation through scripts/mutation-run.sh (#36) — it clears both results dirs, passes --continue, and refuses XML older than the run; do not hand-roll the gradle invocation. Full defect-class canon: docs/canon.md.
run full test suite, report pass/fail
post review to GitHub: gh pr review --comment with formatted checklist and findings
save to pr/feedback/ if directory exists

persist the mutation table to `.pipeline-state/<branch>-mutations.md` — a table that exists only in a subagent's report cannot be audited by a later stage, which is exactly how PR #34's uncovered branches survived Implementation.

declare this review's instrument (mutation, differential execution, doc-vs-code read, type-shape read, real-consumer drive). A re-review round must use a DIFFERENT instrument than the previous round — PR #43's `lastOrNull` survived five suite-measuring stages and fell only to differential execution; PR #47's write-path defect was reachable only by reading the type

re-review the FIX DELTA, not the whole PR — after any round whose fixes changed behavior, review `git diff <pre-fix-sha>..HEAD` alone with a DIFFERENT instrument. The fix diff is the densest defect site in the pipeline: it is written under the framing of the finding rather than fresh, and it is the least-reviewed code in the branch. v0.5.2 evidence: PR #65's round-2 fix introduced the capacity-1 regressions round 3 caught; PR #66's round-2 fix contained four real bugs found by a scoped round 3 at a third of a full round's cost; PR #67's re-review refuted a claim its own fix commit had just introduced.

10.name: Review Verdict
10.note: Verdict is determined by the Code Review subagent above. If APPROVE, proceed to Merge. If REQUEST_CHANGES, fix issues, re-commit, re-push, re-run Code Review.

checklist.action: if REQUEST_CHANGES: fix issues, re-commit, re-push, re-run stage 9

11.name: Merge PR
11.subagent_prompt: Merge PR #{pr_number} in {project_path}. Step 0: Run 'gh pr checks {pr_number}' — verify CI green. If pre-existing failure, document with gh pr comment before merging. Step 1: Run gh pr merge {pr_number} --squash --delete-branch. Do NOT run gh pr review --approve (GitHub blocks self-approval). Output PR_MERGED or MERGE_FAILED.

checklist.action: verify CI green: gh pr checks — if failing for pre-existing reasons, document in PR comment before merging
if the plan defers verification to post-merge observation, perform the observation and post it as a PR comment with the run URL

12.name: Retrospective
12.subagent_prompt: Write retrospective for refactor: {task_description}. Project: {project_path}. PR #{pr_number}. Run 'gh pr view {pr_number} --json commits,title,body' to get PR details (branch deleted after merge). Rate quality 1-5, what went well, lessons learned, improvements. MANDATORY: Post retro as gh pr comment {pr_number} --body '<formatted retro with quality, lessons, improvements>'. MANDATORY: Append to .pipeline-log.md (create if needed, ensure in .gitignore). Your FINAL output line MUST be exactly 'RETRO_COMPLETE'. If this PR closes a milestone, end the retro with a consolidated carry-forward section listing every open item from all the milestone's PR retros, so /pipeline-retro starts from one list.

checklist.action: post retrospective to GitHub PR: gh pr comment
